comment: Source of truth for the phrase-match idiom database. Human-editable. Every source URL must be alive (checked with scripts/verify_refs.py --from-data) before it is committed.

readings.gloss_ru: не торопись, не спеши с действием или решением
readings.gloss_en: don't rush; take your time with an action or decision

analogs.pragmatics: direct appeal to the listener to slow down; closest pragmatic match
warns of the consequences of hurrying; less direct than the Russian imperative

analogs.text: Immer langsam mit den jungen Pferden!
analogs.pragmatics: keeps the horse imagery; direct appeal to slow down

sources.note: dict.cc lists it as equivalent of 'Hold your horses!'

analogs.pragmatics: neutral 'calm down / no rush'; loses the horse imagery

sources.note: dict.cc lists it as equivalent of 'Hold your horses!'

readings.gloss_ru: буквально: не погоняй лошадей (о настоящих лошадях)
readings.gloss_en: literal: do not drive the horses hard (about real horses)

analogs.text: Don't drive the horses so hard.
analogs.pragmatics: plain literal translation; use only when real horses are meant

analogs.text: Treib die Pferde nicht so an.
analogs.pragmatics: plain literal translation; use only when real horses are meant

aliases: от работы кони дохнут, а люди крепнут

readings.gloss_ru: шутливое оправдание нежелания перерабатывать: чрезмерное усердие вредно
readings.gloss_en: jocular justification for not overworking: excessive zeal is harmful

analogs.text: All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.
analogs.pragmatics: same anti-overwork stance but much milder; the Russian original is coarser and more ironic — flag the register gap

analogs.text: Arbeit allein macht auch nicht glücklich.
analogs.pragmatics: same stance, milder tone; dict.cc gives it as the German rendering of 'All work and no play (makes Jack a dull boy)'

sources.note: dict.cc pairing with 'All work and no play (makes Jack a dull boy).'

readings.gloss_en: serious warning: exhausting labor is destructive

sources.note: same proverb; the serious reading is contextual

analogs.text: Working yourself to death helps no one.
analogs.pragmatics: register-matched paraphrase; no established English proverb carries the serious reading with the same force

analogs.text: Man kann sich auch zu Tode arbeiten.
analogs.pragmatics: register-matched paraphrase built on the common verb 'sich zu Tode arbeiten' (to work oneself to death)

без труда не вынешь рыбку из пруда
